note: Both arms get the compiler and are barred from reading the Jet stdlib source, README and docs -- the deployment this skill is for is writing .jet files OUTSIDE a Jet checkout. Compiling is cheap for both arms, so the discriminating assertions are the SILENT traps, which a compiler cannot catch.

evals.name: json-null-config
evals.prompt: JSON config blobs where optional fields come back as JSON null rather than absent. Module `cfg` with `summarize(json_binary)` returning atom-keyed name/retries/tags with defaults for missing OR null.
traps: JSON null decodes to the atom null, not nil
map literal keys are atoms only

assertions.text: cfg.jet compiles
DISCRIMINATING: a JSON null name yields <<"unnamed">>, not the atom null (nil is [], and null is neither)
a present retries (7) is kept, and a missing tags defaults to []
second input: name <<"api">>, retries defaults to 3, tags [<<"a">>,<<"b">>]
the result map's keys are the atoms name/retries/tags (no `unknown`, no char-list keys)
no [x | rest] cons pattern in the source

evals.name: agent-dsl-reviewer
evals.prompt: An agent file: drives claude-code-acp, workspace ./src, expose review(diff) with a typed schema including an enum severity, a shell tool, and an on_approval policy.

assertions.text: reviewer.jet compiles
drives claude-code-acp (or runner Acp(command:))
workspace "./src"
expose review(diff) carries a -> schema rather than being untyped
DISCRIMINATING: severity is expressed as enum(...) of low/medium/high, the mechanism Jet actually checks
a tool with a body that runs a shell command
DISCRIMINATING: the policy is `def on_approval(req)`, not the removed `approve do |req|` form

evals.name: actor-stats
evals.prompt: An actor accumulating numbers: add/mean/reset, plus surviving a bare message.
traps: is_* needs erlang:: outside a guard

assertions.text: stats.jet compiles
DISCRIMINATING: the actor declares an explicit def initialize() (an actor without one dies at spawn)
the demonstrated run prints mean 20 for 10,20,30
after reset, mean prints :none
add returns the running count
an on_message callback exists so a bare message doesn't kill the actor
no [x | rest] cons pattern in the source
DISCRIMINATING: any is_* type test outside a guard is erlang::-qualified

how_to_run: python3 grade.py <iteration-dir>  -- recompiles each produced .jet and drives it with grade.py's own driver; never trusts the agent's self-reported output. See RESULTS.md.
